source.search_operation: One repository-scoped code search for initTransactions + lingering transaction + EXACTLY_ONCE + abort transaction, followed by exact fetch of the single surfaced integration-test source family.

observation: The current surfaced ExactlyOnceKafkaWriter integration-test family contains shouldAbortLingeringTransactions(): a failed writer creates two lingering transactions, writer state carrying the old transactional-id prefix is supplied to restoreWriter(...), and the recovered writer proceeds while the old lingering transactions are aborted/fenced. The same file separately tests testAbortOnClose(), where an orderly writer close aborts an open transaction so a successive writer can commit. Thus the connector has an integrated automatic recovery path when a writer is recreated/restored with the relevant state, plus an orderly-close cleanup path.
failure_boundary: This source family does not show an independent broker-side reconciler that cleans an orphaned EXACTLY_ONCE transaction while the Flink writer/job remains absent after an unexpected stop. Its automatic path is conditioned on creation of a recovered writer with prior state; its close path is conditioned on close() running. Therefore FE-502's manual-tool finding must not be generalized to all recovery, but the specific no-restart/no-close orphan case still has a residual external recovery problem on the evidence inspected here.
falsifying_trace: A new writer is explicitly reconstructed via restoreWriter(...) with KafkaWriterState carrying the old transactional-id prefix.
The recovered writer can write/flush/commit, demonstrating automatic cleanup/fencing during restart/recovery in this tested integration path.
A separate orderly-close test demonstrates automatic abort only when close() executes.
No code in this single inspected source family demonstrates autonomous cleanup while no writer/job instance exists; that absence is not promoted beyond this source family.
exact_scope_guard: Limited to ExactlyOnceKafkaWriterITCase.java at apache/flink-connector-kafka commit dc707db60fcf3c0637114503c27685c881519c2c and the two observed test paths shouldAbortLingeringTransactions/testAbortOnClose. This proves an automatic restart/recovery and orderly-close control in that tested family; it does not prove repository-wide absence or presence of a separate autonomous broker reconciler, does not cover future commits, and does not generalize to all Flink/Kafka transaction recovery.

phase1_assessment.reason: For the exact no-restart/no-close orphan case, this source family exposes no autonomous cleanup witness; the observed automatic path requires a recovered writer/job execution. That application execution is part of normal system recovery, not a Chat-native proof that an absent job's broker postcondition is independently reconciled.

exact_next_action: Fresh-bootstrap next invocation, then inspect exactly one implementation source family behind restored ExactlyOnceKafkaWriter transaction cleanup to identify the precise automatic abort/fencing trigger and whether it can run without writer/job reconstruction. Preserve the no-restart/no-close distinction; one no-match stays search-level only; keep zero-manual, zero-finite-quota and zero-cost gates.
